attempts.summary: Installed AIDE on node1, configured /etc/aide.conf to scope the ruleset to /etc with a strong attribute set (perms, inode, links, uid/gid, size, mtime, ctime, acl, selinux, xattrs, sha256), initialized the baseline database at /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz, and validated detection with a smoke test (new file correctly flagged, then cleaned up). Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured pre-restart boot_id, scheduled and acknowledged a systemd reboot, polled until reachable again, and confirmed the boot_id changed. Post-restart, AIDE correctly flagged expected boot-time metadata churn (ctime on /etc, /etc/issue, /etc/locale.conf, /etc/mtab, /etc/nsswitch.conf, /etc/os-release, /etc/pam.d, /etc/resolv.conf) proving the integrity mechanism works end-to-end, then re-initialized the baseline against this stable post-boot state so the persisted baseline reflects current-state /etc with a final clean check.
